newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares set another new record all-time high.
newsitem.headline: German shares set another new record all-time high.

text.p: Germany's DAX index showed no signs of giving up momentum on Wednesday as the blue-chip index ended bourse trade at a new record high after breaking the important 4,200-point barrier.
The 30-share DAX index was up 80.11 points at 4,201.24 points after reaching a new all-time high at 4,202.05 points.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was up 58.88 points at 4,198.56 points in post-bourse dealings.
"The buy orders are coming into the market without end," said one Frankfurt dealer. "It's the same thing every day. There are no sell orders, only buyers from a broad spectrum."
The DAX has now set a new record closing high in eight of the 12 trading days so far in July.
Dealers said the DAX was targeting 4,200 points ahead of Friday's expiry of DAX futures options.
One trader said open interest at the 4,200 strike was "very strong" and that the level was "acting like a magnet" in drawing the market to new record highs.
The DAX's upward trend was constantly setting new all-time record highs, which reached a peak at 4,206.05 in the IBIS DAX.
The usual factors -- a firmer dollar and Wall Street gains -- were the driving forces behind the German market's advance.
Export-sensitive shares in the DAX index continued to be strong performers, particularly chemical shares.
Hoechst AG was up 2.68 marks at 84.08 marks after setting a new record high at 84.20 marks, while Bayer AG rose 1.60 marks to 75.60 marks and BASF AG rose 2.15 marks to 70.55 marks.

Lufthansa AG failed to perform with the market, falling five pfennigs to 35.10 marks despite news on Tuesday that the airline said it was in talks to sell its 25 percent stake in airline Cargolux to Swissair.

Karstadt AG was among the best performers, rising 37.50 marks to 663 marks despite market speculation that the retailer will soon be dropped from the DAX index in favour of sportswear group Adidas AG.
Karstadt has gotten a boost from views by analysts that the retailer's restructuring programme has begun to take hold.
